checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, 'I'd bet money' qualifier, axis, horizon and unresolved outcome all match. Two problems: (1) The rationale opens by calling the claim 'plausible'. No evidence item supports that judgement, and the packet lists only gaps. (2) The e1 public excerpt is cut to the single word 'training'. That drops the cited sentence about using Axel Springer content to advance training, so readers can't check what the item says. The e2 excerpt is a fair fragment.

The excerpt, proposition, Q1 2024 interpretation, axis, horizon and unresolved outcome all match. The rationale fairly reflects RBC calling valuations stretched while rejecting a dot-com comparison. But the e1 public excerpt 'Tech Bubble 2.0.' leaves out 'At this stage, we don't think this is'. Without those words the quote reads as the opposite of RBC's actual conclusion, which is that this is not Tech Bubble 2.0. The excerpt must include the negation.
